dictionary.definition: interrogative particle

currentComponents.note: 么 derives from 幺, a pictograph of a small twisted skein of silk thread, symbolizing something tiny or insignificant. As a standalone character it was later borrowed purely for its sound, becoming the light, toneless question particle seen in words like 什么 and 怎么.

dictionary.definition: this, that; single; measure word for individuals

etymology.hint: A tally 丨 of people 人

currentComponents.note: 丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.

dictionary.definition: according to; so as to; because of; then

currentComponents.note: 以 traces back to an ancient pictograph of a person bent over holding a tool or plough. The image of a person using an implement gave rise to its meaning 'to use, by means of, according to.'

dictionary.definition: to do, to act; to handle, to govern; to be

currentComponents.note: 为's traditional form 為 depicted a hand grasping the trunk of an elephant, symbolizing training an elephant to work — the source of 为's meaning 'to do, to act,' and by extension 'for, because of.'

dictionary.definition: self, oneself; personal, private; 6th heavenly stem

etymology.hint: A loom woven with thread

currentComponents.note: 己 is thought to depict a woven cord or thread pattern, though its exact original picture is debated; it came to be used for the reflexive idea of 'oneself.'

dictionary.definition: already; finished; to stop; then, afterwards

currentComponents.note: 已 began as a pictograph closely related to 巳, showing a coiled snake or a tied-off cord. The character was later borrowed phonetically to write the grammatical sense 'already, to stop, to cease,' unrelated to its original picture.

dictionary.definition: should, must; to respond, to handle; to deal with, to cope

currentComponents.note: The base of 应 preserves a trace of 心 (heart, mind), reflecting the traditional 應's link to an inner, felt reaction — the root of meanings like 'to respond' and 'to answer.'
应 simplifies 應, whose original phonetic element was a bird-related term read yīng; that ancient reading survives in one of 应's two modern pronunciations, yīng, as in 应该 (yīnggāi, 'should').

dictionary.definition: affair, matter, business; to serve; accident, incident

currentComponents.note: 事 originally pictured a hand holding a forked tally stick or ceremonial staff, used by officials to record duties. Over time the image was abstracted into a compact character meaning 'affair, matter, to serve.'

dictionary.definition: rare; to hope for, to strive for; to expect

currentComponents.note: 爻 (crossed, interwoven strands) — pictures a loosely woven pattern, the idea of something thin or sparse.
巾 (cloth) — a piece of loosely woven cloth gave 希 its early meaning 'sparse, rare,' which later extended figuratively to 'hope,' something rare and longed for.

dictionary.definition: appropriate, timely; to act, to serve; the sound of bells

currentComponents.note: 当 (simplified from 當) combined 田 (a field) with 尚, and originally referred to comparing two fields to judge whether their value was equal. That sense of correspondence broadened into 当's meanings 'to correspond to, to serve as, to be when.'

dictionary.definition: also, too

currentComponents.note: 也 is thought to have originally been a pictograph of a coiled snake, or possibly a ladle, though scholars disagree on the exact image. Whatever its original referent, the character was borrowed purely for its sound to serve as the grammatical particle meaning 'also, too,' the meaning it retains today.

dictionary.definition: square, rectangle; side; region; flag

currentComponents.note: 方 is thought to have originally pictured a plow or a forked tool with square corners, later extended to describe squareness, direction, and by extension a proper method or way of doing something.

dictionary.definition: no, not, un-; negative prefix

etymology.hint: A bird flying toward the sky 一

currentComponents.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

dictionary.definition: to prepare; to get ready, to equip; ready; perfect

etymology.hint: To go 夂 to the farm 田 to prepare for a harvest

currentComponents.note: 夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

dictionary.definition: rare beast; strange; elegant

etymology.hint: An animal standing straight; 亠 is the head

currentComponents.note: 亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

dictionary.definition: to agree to, to consent, to permit; ready, willing

etymology.hint: To stop 止 flexing one's muscles ⺼

currentComponents.note: 止 depicts a foot coming to a stop.
⺼ (flesh, muscle) — pausing to make an effort willingly gave 肯 its meaning 'to be willing, to agree.'

dictionary.definition: clear; to finish; particle of completed action

etymology.hint: A child swaddled in blanklets; compare 子

currentComponents.note: Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

dictionary.definition: to thrive, to prosper, to flourish
in front, forward; former, preceding

currentComponents.note: 止 (foot) at the top of 前 shows movement.
舟 (boat) beneath the foot completes the original picture of a foot stepping into a boat to move ahead, which is how 前 came to mean 'front' or 'before.'

dictionary.definition: to go away, to leave, to depart

currentComponents.note: 土 here is a worn-down form of 大, a person — in the oracle-bone form of 去, a figure is shown stepping away from an opening.
厶 represents a pit or opening the figure above is moving away from, giving 去 its meaning 'to leave, to go.'

dictionary.definition: again, twice, re-

etymology.hint: Two fish 冉 caught on a line 一

currentComponents.note: 再 depicts something stacked again on top of a base line — repetition, or doing something 'once more,' is pictured by piling on an extra layer.

dictionary.definition: scholar, gentleman; soldier

currentComponents.note: 士 is thought to originate as a pictograph of a ceremonial battle-axe, a symbol of rank carried by men of standing, which broadened to mean 'gentleman, scholar, soldier.' A popular but unrelated folk reading splits it into 十 (ten) plus 一 (one), someone who 'knows everything from one to ten.'

dictionary.definition: clear, distinct; pain, suffering; surname
no, not; lacking, -less

currentComponents.note: 无 (a simplified form of 無) originally depicted a person holding ornamented sleeves or plumes while dancing; the character was borrowed for its sound to mean 'nothing, without,' and the dance meaning was later given its own character, 舞.

dictionary.definition: clothes; to dress, to wear; to take medicine

etymology.hint: A person 卩 putting on 又 a coat 月

currentComponents.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

dictionary.definition: to change, to transform, to alter; rebel

currentComponents.note: 变 is the simplified form of 變, whose traditional structure combined 言 (speech) with 攴 (a hand holding a tool) — the idea of altering something through repeated action and effort gave 变 its meaning 'to change, to transform.'

dictionary.definition: to lose; to make a mistake, to neglect

etymology.hint: Something 丿 falling from a hand 夫

currentComponents.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'

dictionary.definition: to dislike, to detest; to reject; to satiate

etymology.hint: cliff

currentComponents.note: 厂 (a cliff shape) reflects 厌's original meaning related to a rock formation, later shifted to mean "to dislike."
犬 (quǎn) gives a sound distantly related to yàn, having drifted apart over time.

dictionary.definition: out, outside, external; foreign; in addition

etymology.hint: Night-time 夕 divinations 卜; the supernatural, the foreign

usedInWords.meaning: outside (also pr. [wai4 mian5] for this sense)

currentComponents.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

dictionary.definition: sound, noise; voice, tone, music

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 聲; see that character for the etymology

currentComponents.note: 声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

dictionary.definition: to subdue, to restrain, to overcome; used in transliterations

etymology.hint: A weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄

currentComponents.note: 十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

dictionary.definition: although, even though
long ago; a long time

currentComponents.note: 久's ancient form has been interpreted as a person being held back or supported from behind, an image of delay or duration that gave the character its meaning 'a long time.'

dictionary.definition: death, destruction; to lose; to perish

etymology.hint: A man 人 in a coffin; see 亾

currentComponents.note: 亡 is traditionally read as a person enclosed within a coffin or hidden away — an early image behind its meaning 'to die, to be lost.'

dictionary.definition: another; separate, other
agent, go-between, intermediary; to introduce; shell, armor

etymology.hint: A border 八 dividing people 人

currentComponents.note: 人 (person) forms the top of the character.
八, shown here as a dividing line, suggests separation or a boundary — together with 人 above, giving 介 its meaning 'to lie between, to introduce.'

dictionary.definition: to kill, to murder, to slaughter; to hurt

etymology.hint: To kill 乂 someone and bury them in a coffin 木

currentComponents.note: 乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

dictionary.definition: head; chief, boss; first, top

etymology.hint: high

currentComponents.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

dictionary.definition: to use, to employ, to apply; use

currentComponents.note: 用's oracle-bone form is thought to depict either a wooden bucket or a tortoise-shell prepared for divination; the character was later used to mean 'to use, to employ.'

dictionary.definition: category, class, group, kind; similar to; to resemble
skill, art; method, technique; trick

currentComponents.note: 术 began as a pictograph of a millet plant with grains hanging from its stalk. In the traditional character 術 (skill, technique), this millet sign sat inside 行 (a crossroads radical) as a sound element; simplified Chinese later kept just the millet shape to stand for the whole idea of 'technique' or 'art.'

dictionary.definition: to undertake, to bear, to accept a duty; inheritance

etymology.hint: Three hands 手 lifting a dead body 了

currentComponents.note: 承 depicts multiple hands supporting and lifting something from below — giving 承 its meaning 'to support, to receive, to inherit.'

dictionary.definition: favor, fortune, luck; surname

etymology.hint: Two men, one alive 土 and one dead 干; the living one is lucky

currentComponents.note: The upper part, related to 土, traditionally depicted one person's fate.
干 depicted a contrasting fate — the character set two outcomes side by side, with the fortunate one giving 幸 its meaning 'lucky, fortunate.'

dictionary.definition: city, town; market, fair; to trade

currentComponents.note: 亠 depicts a flag or marker raised above a trading spot.
巾 (cloth) — goods laid out for sale beneath the flag, together giving 市 its meaning 'market, city.'

dictionary.definition: difference, gap; almost, nearly; in error; an officer

etymology.hint: Work 工 done by a sheep 羊; incompetence

currentComponents.note: 羊 (sheep) — work involving livestock, done imperfectly
工 (work) — the labor itself, linked to the idea of falling short

dictionary.definition: measure, volume; amount, quantity

etymology.hint: unit

currentComponents.note: 里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

dictionary.definition: strict, rigorous, rigid; stern

currentComponents.note: 严 is the simplified form of 嚴, which stacked two mouths (吅, shouting) over a cliff 厂 alongside 敢 ('to dare') — commands barked out from a dangerous, elevated post, an image of discipline under pressure. Simplification kept only a compact shell of that picture.

dictionary.definition: noon; 7th terrestrial branch

currentComponents.note: 午 was originally a pictograph of a wooden pestle used for pounding grain. The character was later borrowed for its sound to label the seventh of the twelve earthly branches, which corresponds to the 'horse' hour and, by extension, noon.

dictionary.definition: to make a move, to take action

currentComponents.note: The upper part of 着 is a graphic simplification that grew out of 著's top elements (艹 plus 者); over the centuries the two characters split apart, with 著 keeping 'to write' and 着 taking on 'wearing, attached to, in the process of.'
目 (eye) — an eye fixed on something conveys attention landing on or attaching to a target, echoed in 着's senses 'to touch, to arrive at, to wear.'

dictionary.definition: to doubt, to question, to suspect

etymology.hint: An old man walking 疋 while holding 匕 a cane 矢

currentComponents.note: 疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
